<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915124_theRebbe_182" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915124_theRebbe_182__p006">
  <section v="15">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the blessing "and Hashem blessed him" is a higher level than "found a hundred gates," drawing on the Midrash that Hashem tests a person before elevating them, as with Avraham and Yitzchak, and the Tzemach Tzedek's explanation that "bakol" refers to the innermost aspect of Kesser, a level beyond the reach of arousal from below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And the verse continues, "and Hashem blessed him,"</t>
    <t s="2">which is a level even higher than "found a hundred gates."</t>
    <t s="3">And this will be understood by prefacing what is stated in the Midrash:45</t>
    <t s="4">The Holy One, blessed be He, does not elevate a person to a position of authority until He examines and tests him, etc.,</t>
    <t s="5">and so you find with Avraham Avinu, the Holy One, blessed be He, tested him with ten trials, and he withstood them, and afterwards He blessed him, as it is stated:46</t>
    <t s="6">"And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything [bakol],"</t>
    <t s="7">and likewise Yitzchak, He tested him in the days of Avimelech, and he withstood his test, and afterwards He blessed him, as it is stated: "And Yitzchak sowed in that land, and Hashem blessed him."</t>
    <t s="8">And the Tzemach Tzedek explains47</t>
    <t s="9">regarding the matter of "And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything [bakol],"</t>
    <t s="10">that "bakol" is the innermost aspect of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="11">for in that level,</t>
    <t s="12">arousal from below does not reach there,</t>
    <t s="13">and after Avraham withstood the ten trials, corresponding to the ten Sefiros in which arousal from below is relevant,</t>
    <t s="14">then He blessed him with "bakol,"</t>
    <t s="15">the innermost aspect of Kesser.</t>
    <t s="16">And based on this, it can also be said regarding "and Hashem blessed him" stated about Yitzchak after he withstood his test,</t>
    <t s="17">that "and Hashem blessed him" is a blessing and drawing down from a place where arousal from below does not reach.</t>
    <t s="18">And this is the addition of "and Hashem blessed him" over "found a hundred gates,"</t>
    <t s="19">for "found a hundred gates" is a drawing down through arousal from below,48</t>
    <t s="20">except that the drawing down is disproportionate to the arousal from below.</t>
    <t s="21">And therefore it is stated "found a hundred gates,"</t>
    <t s="22">that Yitzchak found them through his arousal from below.</t>
    <t s="23">And after this it says "and Hashem blessed him" — a blessing and drawing down from above, from its own side,</t>
    <t s="24">"and Hashem blessed him."49</t>
  </section>
  <section v="16">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the threefold expression "great" in the verse "and the man grew, and he went on growing until he became very great" corresponds to the three matters of sowing, finding, and blessing, representing the levels of surrounding light, encompassing light, and the essence (Atzmus).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the verse continues, "and the man grew, and he went on growing until he became very great,"</t>
    <t s="1">where the language "great" is stated three times.</t>
    <t s="2">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="3">that these three "greats" correspond to the three matters of "and he sowed," "and he found," and "and He blessed him."</t>
    <t s="4">"And the man grew" is the drawing down proportionate to the arousal from below</t>
    <t s="5">("and he sowed"),</t>
    <t s="6">which in general is the drawing down of the light that fills [worlds].</t>
    <t s="7">"And he went on growing" is the drawing down disproportionate to the arousal from below</t>
    <t s="8">("and he found"),</t>
    <t s="9">which in general is the drawing down of the encompassing light.</t>
    <t s="10">And therefore it is stated "went on growing,"</t>
    <t s="11">for the concept of "going" is in the encompassing light, which is above the chain of descent.50</t>
    <t s="12">"Became very great" is the drawing down from the place where arousal from below does not reach</t>
    <t s="13">("and Hashem blessed him"),</t>
    <t s="14">which in general is the drawing down of the Essence [Atzmus].</t>
    <t s="15">And therefore it is stated "very great,"</t>
    <t s="16">for the true concept of "without limit"</t>
    <t s="17">("very")</t>
    <t s="18">is in the Essence.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
